_metadata.independence: I read only u10-blind-input.json; no other file, repository search, web lookup or API was used.

hints.reason: Bridges are famously strung with lights (bridge lights), and night-lights / lights coming on at night reach NIGHT; the shared scene is a bridge lit up at night.

best_available.why: One familiar picture, a lit bridge at night, carries both words.

pairs.pair_note: Single hint, solid shared scene.

hints.reason: Bay Bridge (San Francisco) is a famous compound for BRIDGE; a bay is an inlet of the ocean for OCEAN.

best_available.why: Compound on one side, geography on the other; both routes are everyday knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: A plank bridge / wooden-plank footbridge reaches BRIDGE; walking the plank is the stock pirate scene for PIRATE.
A ship's bridge (the command deck) reaches BRIDGE; pirate ship is the obvious compound for PIRATE.

best_available.why: Pirate ship is instant and the ship's bridge is a well-known second sense of bridge.

pairs.pair_note: Two good hints with different routes.

hints.reason: Queensboro Bridge is a real New York bridge for BRIDGE, but the hint literally contains QUEEN (via Queens), which is a rule failure, and the name is only known locally.
London Bridge (the nursery rhyme and the landmark) reaches BRIDGE; the Queen of England / Buckingham Palace in London reaches QUEEN.

best_available.why: Both routes are world-famous and neither needs the other explained.

pairs.pair_note: QUEENSBORO should be removed for containing the target; LONDON is strong enough on its own.

hints.reason: Rope bridge is a stock image for BRIDGE; the ropes of a boxing ring (on the ropes) reach RING through a familiar scene, though a player must think of boxing.

best_available.why: The only hint; the boxing-ring ropes make the RING side recognizable even if not the first association.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: the RING side relies on the boxing scene; a second opinion could call this BORDERLINE.

hints.reason: Data the android on the bridge of the Enterprise reaches ROBOT easily (and robots process data), but BRIDGE is only reached if the player already has Star Trek in mind.
Steel bridge is a standard compound for BRIDGE; robots are stereotypically built of steel (Real Steel, man of steel imagery) for ROBOT, a defensible shared-material route.

best_available.why: Both words are things made of steel in everyone's mental picture; no story has to be supplied.

pairs.pair_note: DATA is clever but the bridge half depends on a franchise frame the hint does not supply.

hints.reason: Stone bridge is a classic compound for BRIDGE; stone is a near-synonym of ROCK, which makes that side trivial but not unfair.
Arch bridge reaches BRIDGE directly; natural rock arches (Arches National Park, sea arches) reach ROCK as a recognizable formation.

best_available.why: Unmissable on both sides; the synonym flag is a note, not a defect under this rubric.

pairs.pair_note: Both work; STONE is the safer serve.

hints.reason: Compass rose is a strong compound for ROSE; BRIDGE is reached only by knowing the compass sits on a ship's bridge, a nautical step most players will not make unprompted.
Arch bridge reaches BRIDGE; a rose arch (garden arch covered in climbing roses) is a familiar scene for ROSE.

best_available.why: Both sides are literal, familiar arches.

pairs.pair_note: COMPASS is a nice idea whose bridge half is too nautical to stand alone.

hints.reason: Rusting steel bridges are a familiar image for BRIDGE; road salt and sea salt causing rust is common knowledge for SALT, and the two combine into one scene.
The road sign Bridge Ices Before Road reaches BRIDGE; salting roads to melt ice reaches SALT.
An old salt is a sailor (idiom) for SALT and a sailor stands on the ship's bridge for BRIDGE, but each half needs a secondary sense and together they feel assembled.

best_available.why: Winter-road scene that everybody has met: bridges ice, salt melts it.

pairs.pair_note: Two good hints; SAILOR is defensible but weaker than either.

hints.reason: London Bridge is falling down and bridge collapses reach BRIDGE; a shadow falls across something is an everyday verb phrase for SHADOW.
Under the bridge (trolls, the song) is a stock phrase for BRIDGE; under the shadow of / in the shadow reaches SHADOW.
Troll under the bridge is excellent for BRIDGE, but nothing recognizable ties a troll to SHADOW; the shadow half is filler.
Hand shadows / shadow puppets reach SHADOW strongly; a bridge hand (the card game) reaches BRIDGE through ordinary usage, though the player must switch senses.

best_available.why: Under the bridge and in the shadow are both idioms a player meets constantly.

pairs.pair_note: TROLL should go; HAND depends on the card-game sense of bridge, worth a second look.

hints.reason: Bay Bridge reaches BRIDGE; SHARK is reached only through sharks sighted in a bay or the Australian place-name Shark Bay, neither of which a player would name readily.

best_available.why: Only hint; the shark half is a thin coastal association rather than a shared scene.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair wants something like FIN or CARD (card shark / bridge the card game) that reaches both sides.

hints.reason: Cable bridge / cable-stayed bridge reaches BRIDGE; SNAKE is reached only through cables snaking across a floor (snake as a verb), a looser link than the rope-looks-like-a-snake image.
Bridge over a river is the default bridge scene; the Snake River and rivers that snake through valleys reach SNAKE by name and by verb.
Rope bridge reaches BRIDGE; the coiled rope mistaken for a snake is a recognizable shape likeness for SNAKE but not a scene or phrase most players would reach for.

best_available.why: Reaches SNAKE two ways (place-name and verb) and BRIDGE instantly.

pairs.pair_note: ROPE and CABLE lean on the same shape likeness; keep RIVER.

hints.reason: Suspension bridge is the obvious compound for BRIDGE; a spider hanging suspended on its thread, or webs likened to suspension bridges, reaches SPIDER only with some reconstruction.

best_available.why: Only hint; the spider half is a plausible image but not a phrase anyone uses.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. WEB or SILK/THREAD-style hints would serve this pair better.

hints.reason: Bridge over water reaches BRIDGE; spring water is a standard compound for SPRING.
Springs bounce, which nails SPRING, but bridges are not thought of as bouncing; the BRIDGE half is absent.
Suspension bridge reaches BRIDGE; a car's suspension is made of springs, reaching SPRING.

best_available.why: Both sides are direct, well-known senses with no filler.

pairs.pair_note: Drop BOUNCE; the other two are strong.

hints.reason: Star Trek is an instant compound for STAR; the bridge of the Enterprise is the franchise's most famous set, reaching BRIDGE through the same story.

best_available.why: A single world-famous story holds both words.

pairs.pair_note: Both halves travel through one franchise, which the rubric accepts (cf. POISON for APPLE+QUEEN).

hints.reason: A trestle is a type of bridge for BRIDGE and railway trestles carry trains for TRAIN; the word itself is a little less everyday.
Railroad bridge reaches BRIDGE; railroad train reaches TRAIN.

best_available.why: Plain compound on both sides, universally known.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair.

hints.reason: Bridges cross rivers for BRIDGE; river water for WATER.
Bridge Over Troubled Water is a famous song title containing both targets in one phrase.

best_available.why: One iconic phrase names the whole pair.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Bridge over a river reaches BRIDGE; WITCH is reached only via witch-ducking in rivers, a historical detail players would not recall from the word RIVER.

best_available.why: Only hint, and the witch half is effectively missing.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Something like HAG/TROLL-adjacent folklore or WICKED-style stories would need a hint that actually meets WITCH; RIVER does not.

hints.reason: A bridge crossing is a direct compound for BRIDGE; WOLF is reached only through wildlife-crossing signs or Red Riding Hood crossing the woods, neither of which names a wolf.

best_available.why: Only hint; the wolf half is a weak animal-crossing association.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair lacks a natural shared scene; consider retiring it or finding a story that holds both (e.g. Billy Goats Gruff would be TROLL, not WOLF).

hints.reason: The king is a playing card for CARD; kings live in castles for CASTLE.
House of cards is an iconic phrase for CARD; a castle is a grand house (a man's home is his castle) for CASTLE.

best_available.why: Both halves are immediate and concrete.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Wild card for CARD; wildcat for CAT.

best_available.why: Two everyday compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: The queen is a playing card for CARD; a queen wears a crown for CROWN.
The king is a playing card for CARD; a king wears a crown for CROWN.

best_available.why: Marginally the more default royal; either serves.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints are the same route; interchangeable.

hints.reason: The ace is a playing card for CARD; ace of diamonds is a familiar phrase for DIAMOND.
Cards come in suits for CARD; diamonds is one of the four suits for DIAMOND.

best_available.why: Cleanest: diamonds are literally a suit of cards.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Wild card for CARD; wild dog is a familiar compound for DOG.
Poker is a card game for CARD; the Dogs Playing Poker paintings are a famous shared scene for DOG.

best_available.why: A single famous image holds both words.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Magic card tricks and the card game Magic: The Gathering reach CARD; dragons belong to the magic / fantasy world for DRAGON.

best_available.why: Fantasy frame reaches both, with the trading-card game as a bonus.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Easter card (greeting card) for CARD; Easter egg for EGG.

best_available.why: One holiday, two compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Wild card for CARD; wildfire for FIRE.

best_available.why: Two everyday compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Go Fish is a children's card game, reaching CARD through the game and FISH through its name.

best_available.why: The phrase Go Fish is the pair.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Halloween greeting cards reach CARD, a lesser-known holiday-card category; ghosts are the Halloween icon for GHOST.

best_available.why: The ghost half is unmissable and holiday cards are a known route.

pairs.pair_note: Card side is the weaker, but recognizable.

hints.reason: House of cards for CARD; glass house (people in glass houses) for GLASS.

best_available.why: Two idioms, both universal.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Credit card for CARD; the Gold Card tier of credit cards (Amex Gold and the like) reaches GOLD as a familiar phrase.

best_available.why: Gold card is a well-worn phrase, so the pair is reachable.

pairs.pair_note: Gold half depends on the credit-card tier; a second reviewer might call it BORDERLINE.

hints.reason: Cards come in suits for CARD; hearts is a suit for HEART.
Valentine card for CARD; the Valentine heart for HEART.

best_available.why: A single scene most people have lived.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair.

hints.reason: Valentine card for CARD; honey as the pet name for your Valentine / sweetheart reaches HONEY through the endearment sense.

best_available.why: Only hint; the endearment route is recognizable if not literal.

pairs.pair_note: Honey half rides on the pet-name sense; acceptable but not strong.

hints.reason: The race card (the day's list of races, and the idiom playing the race card) reaches CARD; horse race reaches HORSE directly.

best_available.why: Horse race is instant and race card is a real phrase on both sides of the Atlantic.

pairs.pair_note: Card half leans on an idiom; fine.

hints.reason: Hockey trading cards reach CARD; ice hockey reaches ICE.

best_available.why: Compound on both sides.

best_available.why: One sport supplies both words.

hints.reason: The hotel key card is a single object that is both a card and a key.

best_available.why: The two targets literally form the compound key card at a hotel.

hints.reason: Deck of cards reaches CARD; KING is reached because the king is a card in the deck, so the hint names the container of both targets.
Hearts is a card suit and game for CARD; king of hearts is a stock phrase for KING.

best_available.why: King of hearts is a phrase; DECK only reaches KING through CARD.

pairs.pair_note: DECK is near one-sided (king only via being a card); flagged for a second opinion.

hints.reason: Tarot cards reach CARD instantly; the Knight is a court card in every tarot suit, reaching KNIGHT for anyone who has seen a deck.

best_available.why: Card half is immediate and the knight court card is a real feature of the deck.

pairs.pair_note: Knight half is a little specialist; acceptable.
